payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Are visible pencil-like contours or tonal strokes present in any localized part of the edited image, replacing photographic rendering there?
node.criteria: Compare SOURCE and EDITED for localized evidence of the requested pencil-drawing transformation. Credit visible graphite-like contours or pencil-like tonal strokes or shading that replace photographic rendering in a portion of the scene, such as the food or dishes. Muted color, grain, blur, or softened photographic edges alone are not pencil-specific treatment. This check records localized evidence only; it does not establish that the whole image is rendered as a pencil drawing.
node.binding: Compare SOURCE with EDITED: identify whether any localized part of the source scene has visible graphite-like contours or pencil-like tonal strokes replacing photographic rendering. Do not count desaturation, grain, blur, or softened edges alone.
node.source_quote: Change the image into pencil drawing
node.endpoint: Visible pencil-specific treatment replaces photographic rendering in at least one localized part of the image.
node.necessity: Auxiliary evidence check for whether the requested transformation has made localized progress; it does not replace or weaken the required whole-image endpoint.
node.zero_when: No localized pencil-specific contours or tonal strokes replacing photographic rendering are visible; changes are limited to desaturation, grain, blur, or softened photographic edges.
node.half_when: Pencil-specific contours or tonal strokes replace photographic rendering in a limited portion, while other visible portions remain photographic or merely softened.
node.full_when: Clear pencil-specific contours or tonal strokes replace photographic rendering in multiple localized portions of the scene; this auxiliary endpoint does not by itself mean the whole-image transformation is complete.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows localized pencil-like tonal shading and sketchy contours on the food and dishes, especially the meat, vegetables, and plate, replacing some of their photographic appearance. Other areas, including the glassware and table setting, remain largely photographic or softened, so the localized treatment is limited rather than clearly present across multiple portions.
